💰 Bitcoin is back above $75,000. What changed?

Bitcoin has extended its recovery after breaking above $70,000 for the first time since June.

At the time of publication, BTC is trading near $76,000.

The rally followed several developments:

• the US Treasury announced plans to double buybacks of long-duration government debt
• the move briefly reduced pressure in the bond market and supported risk assets
• President Trump urged Congress to advance the Clarity Act
• a wave of short-covering added momentum to the price increase

Short-covering happens when traders betting on a decline buy Bitcoin to close their positions. That additional demand can accelerate an upward move.

However, this type of forced buying eventually slows down. For the rally to continue, the market will need sustained demand beyond short-covering alone.

A breakout shows momentum.

What happens after the breakout shows whether that momentum is sustainable.

The Enoch Scrolls

Be Careful Where You Pour

For a long time, I thought loving like Jesus meant continuing to pour.

Pour more grace.
Give another chance.
Forgive one more time.
Keep showing up.

But God has been teaching me something:

He calls us to love everyone.
He does not call us to give everyone unlimited access to us.

There is a difference between having a forgiving heart and continually placing that heart into hands that have shown they will mishandle it.

Forgiveness can be given freely.

Trust is built.
Access is chosen.

Even Jesus loved everyone, yet He did not entrust Himself to everyone. He knew when to stay, when to speak, when to remain silent, and when to walk away.

Maybe spiritual maturity isn’t learning how to pour more.

Maybe it’s learning to ask God:

“Father, where do You want me to pour?”

Because our time is precious.
Our energy is precious.
Our love is precious.
Our peace is precious.

And pouring endlessly into places God never asked us to remain can leave us too empty to pour into the places He actually assigned to us.

So love freely.

Forgive freely.

Carry no bitterness.

But ask God for discernment before handing someone continued access to your heart, your peace, and your life.

Sometimes the most loving thing you can do is forgive someone completely…

and stop pouring.

Prayer

Father, give me a heart that loves without bitterness and forgives without keeping score. But also give me wisdom and discernment. Show me where You are asking me to pour and where You are asking me to step away. Teach me the difference between forgiveness and access, between grace and enabling, between loving someone and losing myself trying to save them.

Help me protect the peace You have given me without hardening my heart.

May I pour generously—but only where You lead.

Amen.
